shell.studio.overview.kind.entity: The records the application keeps, and their fields.
shell.studio.overview.kind.seed: Records the application starts with, such as its departments.
shell.studio.overview.kind.sequence: Business numbers such as PR-2026-00042, handed out with no gaps.
shell.studio.overview.kind.dataSource: A query over entities that tables, charts and KPIs show.
shell.studio.overview.kind.site: Where people use the application: its address, navigation and languages.
shell.studio.overview.kind.page: A screen of a site, built from widgets.
shell.studio.overview.kind.form: How a record is entered and edited, in sections or steps, with conditions.
shell.studio.overview.kind.process: The steps a record goes through, such as an approval, with tasks for people.
shell.studio.overview.kind.rule: A reusable expression that validations, filters and processes call.
shell.studio.overview.kind.role: A part people play, such as a manager, that tasks and policies name.
shell.studio.overview.kind.policy: What each role may read and change, record by record.
shell.studio.overview.kind.identityProvi: How the application's people sign in.
shell.studio.overview.kind.connector: Calls to another system, with its address and sign-in.
shell.studio.overview.kind.endpoint: Lets another system create a record and start a process in one call.
shell.studio.overview.kind.text: The words of the application in one more language.
shell.studio.overview.kind.scenario: A test that runs the application's steps and checks the results.
shell.studio.overview.kind.migration: Changes one entity's stored data in a way adding cannot, such as renaming a field.
shell.studio.overview.kind.event: A named event about one entity, which processes raise and other systems receive.
shell.studio.overview.kind.trigger: Starts a process for a record when something happens, such as on a schedule.
shell.studio.overview.kind.webhook: Sends an event to another system's address, signed so it can check the sender.
shell.studio.overview.when.entity: You need one for each kind of record people keep, such as a request or an asset.
shell.studio.overview.when.seed: Handy for lists that must be ready on the first day, such as leave types or currencies.
shell.studio.overview.when.sequence: For records people quote by their number, such as an invoice or a ticket.
shell.studio.overview.when.dataSource: Use one when a table, chart or KPI shows records filtered, joined or totalled.
shell.studio.overview.when.site: A second site gives another group of people, such as suppliers, their own address and menu.
shell.studio.overview.when.page: Every screen people open from the navigation is a page.
shell.studio.overview.when.form: Worth adding when entering or reviewing a record needs a layout of its own.
shell.studio.overview.when.process: Approvals, and any other steps a record goes through, are built as a process.
shell.studio.overview.when.rule: Write a condition or a calculation once, then use it wherever it is needed.
shell.studio.overview.when.role: Each part people play that sees or does something different, such as a manager, is a role.
shell.studio.overview.when.policy: Needed as soon as a role may see or change only some records or fields.
shell.studio.overview.when.identityProvi: For people who sign in with their company's own accounts.
shell.studio.overview.when.connector: Reach for one when the application reads from or writes to another system.
shell.studio.overview.when.endpoint: When a partner system sends records in, it calls an endpoint.
shell.studio.overview.when.text: One for each further language people use the application in.
shell.studio.overview.when.scenario: Keeps a behaviour working as the application changes: one scenario for each behaviour that matters.
shell.studio.overview.when.migration: Seldom by hand: the entity designer writes one whenever a change it saves needs it.
shell.studio.overview.when.event: Lets other systems and processes hear that something happened to a record.
shell.studio.overview.when.trigger: For a process that starts on its own, on a schedule or when a record changes.
shell.studio.overview.when.webhook: For a system that must hear of an event the moment it happens.
